holidays.name: Don't Step on a Bee Day
holidays.description: A buzzing public service announcement in holiday form. Slip on some shoes before wandering through the clover, and give the bees some space. Barefoot summer strolls are lovely, but they're no fun for you or the bee.
holidays.origin: This tongue-in-cheek observance was created by the Wellcat.com holiday site, which is known for wacky, offbeat days. It started as a reminder to wear shoes outdoors. It has since grown into a nudge to protect bees and other pollinators.
holidays.funFact: A honeybee that stings a person usually dies afterward, because its barbed stinger stays lodged in the skin. So stepping on a bee is a bad day for both of you.

holidays.name: National Piña Colada Day
holidays.description: A toast to the creamy, tropical blend of rum, coconut and pineapple. Pour one over ice, add a tiny paper umbrella, and pretend the nearest beach is only a few steps away. A virgin version works just as well for a sunny afternoon.
holidays.origin: The piña colada is tied to San Juan, Puerto Rico, where it became a signature drink and later the island's official beverage. This unofficial food-and-drink holiday celebrates the cocktail every July 10.
holidays.funFact: Piña colada is Spanish for "strained pineapple," a nod to the freshly pressed pineapple juice in the original recipe.

holidays.name: Teddy Bear Picnic Day
holidays.description: A day for packing a basket, grabbing your favorite stuffed bear, and heading outside for sandwiches on a blanket. Kids and nostalgic grown-ups are both welcome, and no bear gets left at home.
holidays.origin: The observance draws on the classic song "The Teddy Bears' Picnic," whose melody dates to 1907 and whose lyrics were added in the 1930s. It's an unofficial holiday that has long been celebrated on July 10.
holidays.funFact: The teddy bear is named after U.S. President Theodore "Teddy" Roosevelt, who famously refused to shoot a captured bear on a 1902 hunting trip.
